options.why: Assumed any net containing triangles must be a pyramid; a pyramid has one base with triangles meeting at an apex, not two separate triangular ends.

questions.solution_text:
The net has two identical triangular ends joined by three rectangles.
Two identical polygons joined by rectangles fold up into a prism named after that polygon.
The solid is a triangular prism.

questions.question_text: How many rectangles are in the net of a hexagonal prism?

options.why: Counted the two hexagons as well as the rectangles ($6+2$).
Doubled the number of sides, as if each side needed two rectangles.
Counted the two end faces instead of the rectangles.

questions.solution_text:
A hexagon has $6$ sides, so $n=6$.
The net has one rectangle for each side of the base.
Rectangles $= n$
$= 6$

questions.question_text: How many edges does a pentagonal prism have?

options.why: Used vertices $=2n$ instead of edges $=3n$.
Used faces $=n+2$ instead of edges $=3n$.
Counted only the edges of one pentagonal end.

questions.solution_text:
A pentagon has $5$ sides, so $n=5$.
Edges $= 3n$
$= 15$

questions.question_text: How many vertices does a hexagonal prism have?

options.why: Counted the vertices of only one hexagonal end.
Used faces $=n+2$ instead of vertices $=2n$.
Used edges $=3n$ instead of vertices $=2n$.

questions.solution_text:
A hexagon has $6$ sides, so $n=6$.
Vertices $= 2n$
$= 12$

questions.question_text:
A triangular prism has a base triangle with sides $5$ cm, $12$ cm and $13$ cm, and the prism is $10$ cm long.
One of its rectangular faces measures $12$ cm by $10$ cm.
Which side of the triangle does that rectangle fold onto?

options.why: $10$ cm is the length of the prism, not a side of the triangular base.
The rectangle's width $12$ cm matches the $12$ cm side, not the $13$ cm side.
The $5$ cm side folds onto the $5$ cm by $10$ cm rectangle instead.

questions.solution_text:
Each rectangle joins one side of the triangle, so its width equals that side and its length equals the prism's length, $10$ cm.
The rectangle is $12$ cm by $10$ cm, so its width is $12$ cm.
It folds onto the $12$ cm side of the triangle.

questions.question_text: Which description correctly gives the faces of the net of a pentagonal prism?

options.why: That describes a pentagonal pyramid, which has one base and triangular sides.
Used $7$ rectangles, but a pentagon has only $5$ sides.
Left out the two pentagonal end faces.

questions.solution_text:
A pentagonal prism has two pentagonal ends and one rectangle for each of the $5$ sides.
So its net is $2$ pentagons and $5$ rectangles.

questions.question_text:
A prism has $24$ edges.
Name the solid.

options.why: Used the pyramid rule edges $=2n$ instead of the prism rule edges $=3n$, giving $2n=24$ and $n=12$.
Ignored the word prism in the stem and applied the pyramid rule edges $=2n$, giving $n=12$ and a pyramid name.
Solved $3n=24$ correctly to get $n=8$, then named the solid a pyramid even though two identical ends joined by rectangles make a prism.

questions.solution_text:
A prism with an $n$-sided base has edges $= 3n$.
$3n = 24$
$n = 8$
The base has $8$ sides, so the solid is an octagonal prism.
